source.value:
Consider the system of linear differential equations given by

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]x(t).
$$

Given that the solution to the system can be written as

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}a \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}a \\ 1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{2t}+[\begin{aligned}b \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}),\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $a+b?$

source.value:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067736/assets/f9f940992f15a14e58f7eee0b8171e8e0e437787d6340618fcd1f23b84d333a8.png)

Since $A$ is upper-triangular, the repeated eigenvalue is $\lambda=-4$ (of multiplicity two).
For this eigenvalue, we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067736/assets/9a7426e0e17bb57e1a8bfb24dca5ca3a579809708af3055184f9cfc2728957bc.png)
So, we get an eigenvector 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067736/assets/f3e3bae74afa48fd689bb48dc317af52e44914f9f35d32375463d3705268b377.png)

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda$ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $\mathbf v,$ the solution of the system of differential equations is given by

$$
\mathbf{x}(t) = c_1\mathbf{v} e^{\lambda t}  + c_2 (\mathbf{v}  te^{\lambda t}  +  \mathbf{w}e^{\lambda t} \, ),
$$

where $\mathbf{w}$ is a solution to the equation $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w}= \mathbf{v}.$

To find $\mathbf{w},$ we solve the equation $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w} = \mathbf{v}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(A-\lambda I)w & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}-4+4 & 1 \\ 0 & -4+4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067736/assets/6e5c9442761d05d62ccc3ce56cbe09794e57b931987e3e4ef33d93d7cfb1e39f.png)

So, we obtain

$$
w_2 = 1.
$$

The variable $w_1$ is a free variable. Setting $w_1 = 0,$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067736/assets/6b54faff854b99c0c86b3de477cc2dde8b5a714bfc296c59ed6757f9bc250f77.png)

Therefore, the general solution is given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067736/assets/96ee1e3a1af5c670b87cd06e406ac16b0fa9f5e5305b2fe95dc395c079d291da.png)

Finally, we see that $a=0, b=1,$ and $a+b=1.$

source.value:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067736/assets/df4b98b4799865dbf40e765bda0fa6176157139d99a62bd1febe48d7c4600c8c.png)

We are given that the eigenvalue is $\lambda=3$ (of multiplicity two). For this eigenvalue, we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067736/assets/8032d75d584838d0743f2e9217c25844af637d07261dd2d6a89add9df531fdb1.png)
So, we get an eigenvector 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067736/assets/aa5146c331315952e36051be1126010bbcaf706f2cbc1c886c56b0e92b468fa4.png)

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda$ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $\mathbf v,$ the solution to the system of differential equations is given by

$$
\mathbf{x}(t) = c_1  \mathbf{v}e^{\lambda t} + c_2 (\mathbf{v}t e^{\lambda t} +  \mathbf{w}e^{\lambda t}),
$$

where $\mathbf{w}$ is a solution to the equation $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w}= \mathbf{v}.$

To find $\mathbf{w},$ we solve the equation $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w} = \mathbf{v}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(A-\lambda I)w & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}-1-3 & -8 \\ 2 & 7-3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-4 & -8 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067736/assets/b0d075668031a0decad6d092f2f03c3f74eacdcff0546e99e8373901c5a910ac.png)

Note that the first equation is a constant multiple of the second. So, we obtain

$$
w_1 =\dfrac{1}{2} - 2 w_2 .
$$

The variable $w_2$ is a free variable. Setting $w_2 = 0,$  we get $w_1 = \dfrac{1}{2},$ and therefore
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067736/assets/726b5737809539337c1a8a259727a47b9bdacdf81de92a4a35783518df9dcaa0.png)

Therefore, the general solution is given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067736/assets/a1a3e46d8352ceee549fb5040261d8edf036d8fb32fc5fc5b960cab07097970f.png)

Now, we need to find the values of $c_1$ and $c_2$ using the initial condition ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14067736/assets/2e3a20e62437546fb2498d1575c9ed2cd268c43b968174ea7e0139977fb6fbd5.png) Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(0) & =[\begin{aligned}-2{c}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{1}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2{c}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{1}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}-2([\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]t{e}^{3t}+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}+[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]t{e}^{3t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(4t-3){e}^{3t} \\ (1-2t){e}^{3t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
